LESSON: ORGANIC GARDENING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES
Topic 2.1: Organic Gardening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Organic Gardening, part of FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we practice organic gardening? 2. How can we produce food crops through organic gardening?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Organic Gardening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: Working collaboratively and organising own learning skills as learners grow crops using organic

gardening practices.

• Self-efficacy: Planning skills as learners grow crops using organic farming practices.

Values:
• Unity: Working in teams as learners undertake the project on growing crops using organic gardening practices.

• Integrity: Honesty as learners practice organic gardening practices.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Food health and safety as learners acquire skills of growing foods without use of agro-chemicals.

Link to other learning areas:

Learners relate organic gardening practices to farming practices in the Social Studies.
